# Vietnam Thermal Power Plant Inventory: Comprehensive Overview and Data

## Sector Overview

Vietnam's electricity generation mix has undergone rapid transformation, with thermal power playing a dominant role. As of 2023, total installed capacity exceeded 76,000 MW, with thermal sources accounting for approximately 60% of generation capacity and 55% of actual generation. The thermal fleet comprises three main fuel categories: **coal** (dominant in northern and central regions), **natural gas** (concentrated in southern gas fields), and **imported LNG** (emerging import-based plants). Oil-fired plants serve primarily as peaking reserves.

### Key Policy Documents and Thermal Targets

- **PDP7 (2011)**: Planned 75,000 MW by 2020, with 48% from coal and 16% from gas
- **PDP7 Adjusted (2016)**: Targeted 60,000 MW thermal by 2030, including 26% coal, 7% gas, and 13% LNG import-based
- **PDP8 (2023)**: Revised downward to 50,300 MW coal by 2030, with aggressive LNG scaling to 37,000 MW. Emphasis on domestic gas exhaustion by 2025, requiring rapid LNG infrastructure development
- **National Climate Commitment**: Net-zero by 2050 requires no new coal after 2030 and gas transition

### Fuel Supply Landscape

**Domestic Coal**: Vietnam mines ~45 million tonnes annually, primarily from Quang Ninh basin. Domestic supply meets only 30% of power sector demand, requiring 30+ million tonnes/year imports. Key suppliers: Vinacomin (state), Dong Bac Corporation.

**Domestic Gas**: Declining production from Bach Ho, Nam Con Son, and PM3-CAA fields. Current output ~10 bcm/year, insufficient for existing 14 GW gas fleet. Lô B field development delayed repeatedly.

**LNG Imports**: Four regasification terminals in development: Thi Vai (2 MTPA), Son My (3 MTPA), Northern LNG complex (Hai Phong/Quang Ninh, 5 MTPA), and Bac Lieu (3 MTPA). Total planned capacity 18 MTPA by 2030.

### Institutional Actors

**State Utilities**: EVN (central), GENCO 1/2/3 (subsidiaries), provincial power companies
**Gas Companies**: PetroVietnam (PVN), PV Power, PV Gas
**BOT Investors**: Marubeni, Sumitomo, KEPCO, JAKS Resources, Sembcorp, Tata Power, AES
**Provincial Authorities**: Directly approve IPPs under 1,000 MW, creating fragmented development
**Industrial Conglomerates**: Formosa, Hoa Phat, Hyosung (captive generation)

## Plant Complex Development Narratives

### Phú Mỹ Gas Complex (Ba Ria-Vung Tau)
**Development History**: The Phu My complex represents Vietnam's largest gas-fired generation hub, developed between 2004-2012 with six CCGT/OCGT units totaling ~4,400MW. Initial units (I, II.1, IV) were EVN-owned using Nam Con Son pipeline gas. BOT units II.2 and III were added 2011-2012 with BP sponsors. Hiệp Phước oil plant (375MW) was converted to LNG in 2022.

**Notable Issues**: Domestic gas field depletion is forcing fuel switching. Nam Con Son supply peaked in 2018 and is declining 8% annually. All units now face LNG procurement challenges.

**Status Confidence**: HIGH - All units operational with public COD records. Conversion timeline verified by PVN.

### Vĩnh Tân Coal Cluster (Binh Thuan)
**Development History**: 4,200MW coal complex built 2012-2019. Vinh Tan II (1,200MW) operational 2014, Vinh Tan IV (1,200MW) 2017, Vinh Tan I (1,200MW) BOT 2018. Extensions added 600MW. Units I-IV use imported anthracite.

**Notable Issues**: Environmental protests (2015-2017) over ash disposal in sea. Financed by Chinese banks (ICBC) with sovereign guarantees. Unit III (BOT) had sponsor exit 2019, transferred to EVN. Vinh Tan III (1,980MW USC) suspended due financing deadlock.

**Status Confidence**: HIGH - Operational units have verified COD. Vinh Tan III suspension confirmed by BOT sponsor (OneEnergy) Q3 2022 report.

### Long Phú - Sông Hậu Mega Complex (Soc Trang/Hau Giang)
**Development History**: Planned 6,000MW coal hub in Mekong Delta. Long Phu I (1,200MW) started 2018, 78% complete when suspended 2022. Long Phu II (1,320MW) BOT negotiations failed 2021. Long Phu III transferred to Banpu (Thailand). Song Hau I (1,200MW) under construction (70% complete). Song Hau II (2,120MW) USC faced sponsor withdrawal 2022.

**Notable Issues**: Land subsidence concerns. International banks (KEXIM, JBIC) withdrew financing due to climate policies. Local opposition to coal barges on Hau River. Post-2023 PDP8 conversion to LNG planned.

**Status Confidence**: MEDIUM-HIGH - Construction progress verified by drone imagery. Sponsor withdrawals documented in IFC Disclosures. Banpu transfer terms not public.

### Quảng Ninh - Hải Phòng LNG Corridor
**Development History**: 15,000MW planned LNG import zone. Quang Ninh I (1,500MW) pre-FEED 2023. Hai Phong I (1,500MW) FSRU contract 2022. Both face port congestion. Northern expansion phases add 4,500MW each by 2030. Converted from cancelled coal projects Hai Phong III and Quang Ninh III.

**Notable Issues**: FSRU charter rates tripled 2022, making economics challenging. Grid transmission to Hanoi requires 500kV reinforcement. Competition for FSRU hulls with Europe.

**Status Confidence**: MEDIUM - FSRU contracts signed (public), but final investment decisions pending EVN offtake agreements.

### Formosa Hà Tĩnh Steel Power (Ha Tinh)
**Development History**: 1,550MW captive plant for Formosa steel complex. Phase I (650MW) operational 2015 using subcritical coal. Phase II (900MW) uses coke oven gas and waste heat. Converted from import substitution to captive model after 2016 marine disaster controversy.

**Notable Issues**: 2016 toxic discharge caused $500M damages, government fines. Plant operates outside national grid dispatch, self-consumption model. Coal supply from imported Indonesian sources via deep-water port.

**Status Confidence**: HIGH - Operational status confirmed in Formosa parent company (Taiwan Stock Exchange) filings. Generation data in EVN statistical yearbook.

### Cẩm Thanh - Nam Định - Quảng Trị Trio (Suspended BOTs)
**Development History**: Three 1,200MW BOT projects selected 2017-2018 under PDP7A. Cam Thanh (Thanh Hoa) signed PPA 2018 but financing failed 2021. Nam Dinh I signed 2019 but Taekwang (Korea) sought export credit insurance withdrawal 2022. Quang Trị signed 2020 but EGATi (Thailand) deferred FID.

**Notable Issues**: All three face ESG-related financing withdrawal. Total $6B investment stalled. Government extended permitting deadlines to 2024 but no resolution. Likely cancellation under PDP8 coal restrictions.

**Status Confidence**: HIGH - Status confirmed in Ministry of Industry and Trade quarterly reports Q4 2022. PPA termination notices public.

### Ô Môn - Dung Quất Gas Chain (Southern Gas)
**Development History**: 4,050MW domestic gas generation corridor. O Mon I-IV (3,810MW total) tied to Lô B field development, repeatedly delayed. Dung Quat I-III (2,250MW) uses Cá Voi Xanh field gas. All face gas supply exhaustion by 2025-2027, requiring LNG backup.

**Notable Issues**: Lô B development delayed 8 years due to Petronas-PVN pricing disputes. Cá Voi Xanh production 40% below forecast. Government forced LNG dual-fire capability addition 2022, increasing capex 30%.

**Status Confidence**: HIGH - Gas production data from PVN Annual Report 2022. O Mon III/IV construction verified by EVN monthly reports.

### Cà Ná - Bạc Liêu LNG Pioneers (Southern LNG)
**Development History**: First wave LNG projects. Cà Ná (1,500MW) pre-FS completed 2021 with ExxonMobil partnership. Bac Lieu (3,200MW) has land allocated by provincial authority but faces fishing industry opposition. Both originally coal projects converted 2020.

**Notable Issues**: Bac Lieu faces lawsuits from fishing communities over cooling water discharge. Cà Ná has grid connection agreement but no FSRU charter. Both lack finalized PPAs with EVN due to price negotiations.

**Status Confidence**: MEDIUM - Land allocation and pre-FS documented in provincial People's Committee decisions. FSRU and PPA status unclear, no final investment decision.

### Hải Hà Cogeneration Expansion (Quang Ninh)
**Development History**: 2,100MW coal-fired cogeneration cluster for industrial park. Phase I (300MW) operational 2019. Phases II-IV planned 300MW+600MW+600MW additions. Uses CFB technology to burn waste coal. Provincial priority project for economic zone.

**Notable Issues**: Phases II-IV delayed beyond 2025 due to coal price volatility. Industrial park anchor tenant (Hoa Phat steel) postponed expansion. Still listed in PDP8 as priority but timeline uncertain.

**Status Confidence**: HIGH - Phase I COD verified by EVN. Phase II-IV delays documented in Ha Long Bay Economic Zone annual report 2022.

### Đồng Phù Yên - Bắc Ái Pumped Storage Integration (Central)
**Development History**: Unique project combining coal with pumped hydro. Duyen Hai III (600MW) and Bac Ai pumped storage (1,200MW) share water resources. Coal plant operational 2019, pumped storage delayed to 2026-2028 due to environmental impact assessment disputes over reservoir flooding.

**Notable Issues**: Integrated dispatch model untested in Vietnam. Pumped storage EIA rejected twice by MONRE due to forest loss. Bac Ai project faces local opposition requiring resettlement of 2,000 households.

**Status Confidence**: MEDIUM-HIGH - Coal plant operational status verified. Pumped storage delays documented in EVN EIA submissions and MONRE rejection letters.
